messages.author: 61221ab1f726dce8
messages.subject: Execute Code in Roxygen Comment
parts:
Hi,

Is there a way for the Vim-R-Plugin to say recognize code that is in an Roxygen2 comment (specifically example section) and be able to run it with like \dd?

For instance, if I had the following Roxygen comments above a R function:

{code}
#' Plot a Cofeature Matrix
#'
#' Generates a ggplot2::geom_tile plot of features by sample.
#' It is able to deal with multiple types affecting the same sample.
#'
#' @param in.df A 3 column (feature, sampleID, type) data.frame object
#' @param feature.order character vector indicating the order of the features
#' in the final plot on the y-axis. If not set, then function will set it
#' automatically
#'
#' @examples
#' v1 <- c("RCOR1", "NCOR1", "LCOR", "RCOR1", "RCOR1", "RCOR1", "RCOR1")
#' v2 <- c("sampleA", "sampleC", "sampleB", "sampleC", "sampleA", "sampleC", "sampleC")
#' v3 <- c("Deletion", "Deletion", "SNV", "Rearrangement", "SNV", "Rearrangement", "SNV")
#' feature.order <- c("RCOR1", "NCOR1", "LCOR")
#' sample.id.order <- c("sampleA", "sampleB", "sampleC")
{/code}

Currently, the #' is recognized as a comment (Roxygen syntax) and Vim-r-plugin will send it to console but it won't get executed.

Thanks.

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: Execute Code in Roxygen Comment
parts:
The Vim-R-plugin already does what you are requesting, but it depends on a very recent syntax/r.vim. See:

https://github.com/jcfaria/Vim-R-plugin/commit/7124e418b2a21d8a48296f0a0bf9262cb1f0d215
https://github.com/jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime/pull/2
https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/2c5e8e80eacf491d4f266983f534a77776c7ae83

That is, you need either to use Vim that include patches at least up to December 5, 2015, or copy the syntax/r.vim from R-Vim-runtime to your Vim installed directory.

messages.author: 61221ab1f726dce8
messages.subject: Re: Execute Code in Roxygen Comment
parts:
Beautiful. Thanks.

For those interested, I ended up using Vundle to install the R-Vim-runtime. Specifically adding to following to my ~/.vimrc:

Plugin 'jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime' "Vim runtime scripts of file types that include R code

Then ran the following in vim:

:PluginInstall
